intent: Start with a symmetric five-sensor baseline ahead of the axle, with 12 mm sensors spaced 8 mm apart. This keeps the row wide enough to cover the 25 mm tape and gives look-ahead for the controller. I have not yet committed to any change. Next, if the Integrator reports that the signal saturates or drops out on tight bends, I am considering widening the sensor row to about 0.024 m half-span, or moving the row further forward (y about 0.06 m) for more look-ahead. If oscillation is high, I am considering a shorter wheel track or lower mass. I expect the baseline to complete the oval and s-bend tracks with a small number of line-loss events, and the slalom to show the main weakness.
learning: No prior race evidence yet. Next iteration, check whether the sensor row saturates (all readings near 1 or all near 0) on each track, and whether line_loss_events cluster on specific bends. Those results will decide whether the row needs to be wider, further forward, or differently sized.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no Geometry Race Data and no Integration Feedback yet, so this proposal rests on design reasoning rather than evidence. Five sensors at 12 mm spacing (x from -0.016 to +0.016 m) span about 48 mm, roughly twice the 25 mm tape width. That gives a steering signal that stays informative when the robot is off-centre and keeps at least one sensor on the tape through moderate bends. Placing the row at y = +0.04 m, ahead of the axle, gives the controller look-ahead so it can react before the wheels reach a bend. Sensor size 0.012 m is about half the tape width: small enough to resolve the edge, large enough that the readings change smoothly. Wheel track 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m are mid-range, giving stable yaw response without excessive turn inertia. Body width 0.12 m sets the off-track limit to max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, which is comfortably above the tape edge. Mass 0.8 kg and body length 0.16 m keep yaw inertia moderate. I expect this baseline to complete the course with a few line-loss events on tight bends. This is a neutral starting point to measure against, not a tuned optimum.
